Hi, we play with a group of 8 of us, so a lot of games end up having issues due to sheer mechanics. I was hoping to get some suggestions for some new games to try out.

Games that we currently play quite a bit even if it is in 2 separate groups:

  • 7 wonders
  • Bang!
  • Ascension
  • Dominion
  • Catan
  • Carcassonne
  • Ticket to Ride
  • Smallworld

I'm really wanting to get the group into some more games similar to Relic or Ninjato(?) but I'm wanting to find a way to play with 8 instead of splitting up. Any advice on games?
Looking for ideas for a larger group of gamers to be able to play together vs. 2 separate games.

Sorry for the late response, but better late than never.

Looking through my played games, there aren't many that accommodate 8 players, but I'll show what I have.

Arkham Horror, Eldritch Horror, and Elder Sign all support up to 8 players. I wouldn't recommend playing with that many though. The game become exponentially easier and longer the more people you play with. With new players you're looking at a 6 hour game easy, no matter which version.

Cash and Guns scales really well with more players, and supports up to 8. Because the game play is mostly real time, adding more players doesn't increase the game time, and there's little waiting for other people. The game is a little bit more on the mean side than the games you play, because you'll be actively choosing which person you want to shoot. This can create some bad times with the wrong group of people, so know your players.

Here's Sit Down and Shut Up's Review of Cash n Guns.

Formula D supports up to Ten players. And boy, can I not recommend playing with that many people. It's a fun press your luck type of game, but playing with more than 5 people really starts to bog the game down. With the right mind set, it can be fun, but having one distracted player will make the game take hours, and that makes it overstay its welcome.

Here's a Tabletop episode of Formula D. Fair warning: they get a handful of rules wrong.

One Night Ultimate Werewolf plays up to 10. I'll go ahead and lump it in with The Resistance. Both games are social deduction games where some players are the bad guys (werewolves or spies) and everyone else is trying to figure out who they are. Highly recommended, and the type of game that can be played over and over. I give One Night a slight lead, because it's all done in one night, and goes much quicker. Thus when someone messes up, it's not too long until the next game starts.

They played The Resistance on Tabletop and One Night Ultimate Werewolf on Board with Life.

Two rooms and a boom supports up to 30 players, and is free to play if you're willing to print n play it. It's similar to the other social games, where the goal is to figure out where everyone's allegiances are, and trying to set the rooms up the way that your team needs to to win. However, I think the game is actually weak with only 8 players. It's still a fun game, but part of the fun is watching that mob mentality occur, and that just doesn't happen with only 4 people in each room.

Board with Life did a video of them playing it

Tsuro is a super awesome abstract game that supports up to 8 players. It's quick to play, and very relaxing. The only real problem is with 8 players you'll be spending quite some time waiting for your turn.

Here's a Tabletop episode of Tsuro

Twilight Imperium supports up to 8 if you get the first expansion. It is the most incredible game, but it could literally take you a whole weekend to play with new players. Not recommended for beginners.

There is no aquequite video to capture Twilight Imperium.

I recently played Spyfall and had a great time with it. From what I understand it's a bit hard to find right now. There is also The resistance which holds up to 10. Both are deceit games but can be great fun with a group who is comfortable with each other.

I used to live in a college town in north Texas (UNT). There was a gas station right next to my apartment complex, literally a 30 second walk from my front door and into the gas station. An illegal Mexican family operated a little taqueria restaurant with 4 tables within. Their menu was only in Spanish, only took cash as payment, and hardly spoke a spick of English.

Their menu consisted of a nice little selection of Spanish food. Pretty much general stuff and maybe a few obscure items that only Hispanics would recognize. They sold breakfast food, such as breakfast burritos and whatnot, but their main menu, which was absolutely fucking delicious, was during lunch.

I remember one day I stopped for some gas, (it happened to be during lunch time) and I noticed the little taqueria place within, but what really caught my attention was the 20 or so people inside waiting in line and eating the food inside. I figured, what the hell, I'm hungry too and decided to eat some good ol' Mexican food.

I waited in line for about 10 minutes and finally ordered some generic chicken tacos (as it was only one of the few items that I could decipher from the menu) and went back to my apartment.

3 tacos for 5 bucks is a damn good deal.

When I finally opened the tacos within the tinfoil wrapped packing, and smelled the food, is when I realized that I was holding something special within my hands. The tortilla was hot and limp within the palm of my hand, casually presenting the food which it braced: small diced chicken, small diced onions, and cilantro.

That was it - 3 ingredients.

It smelled fucking incredible.

Then I opened a small plastic ramekin of salsa, dipped my finger into it, and licked it.

Now I have had my fair share of salsa in my day, everything to homemade to store bought to restaurant brand - and nothing, and I mean nothing compares to this type of salsa which rested within this thin plastic container. It's taste was not too sweet nor too dry. It was the perfect blend of tomato and heat. I love spicy food, but not the stuff that just sets your mouth of fire for the hell of it, but it did have a nice kick to hit. The taste was incredible.

I remember thinking, holy shit that is good.

Then I tasted the taco.

The tortilla and contents were still hot from the tinfoil wrapping, The delectable chicken was cut into tiny bits and pieces, but cooked perfectly and the taste was not lost among the other two ingredients. The onion was the perfect compliment, sauteed, but not over buttered, resting in between the chicken bits and cilantro.

I ate at that little illegal taqueria for months and months, anywhere from 4-6 times per week. Each and every time was perfect.

Then I moved 850 miles away to a place that "has authentic mexican food", but that is a outright, damn fully wrong, bitter FUCKING lie.

I miss that gas station. I miss that illegal mexican family. I miss those fucking tacos.

I remember visiting not too long ago to see family and that shit, but the real reason was to eat those tacos, and going back to the gas station. I ordered some chicken and steak tacos when I last visited.

I cried from joy when I say that sweet lady behind the counter taking orders from everyday customers, I cried when I first bit into that taco, and I balled my eyes out like a little bitch when I finished the meal, because I new it would be at least a year or two when I could eat those tacos again, if they are even cooking them anymore.

That would be my last meal.
